findings.location: Dockerfile FROM build AS publish stage (no ARG VERSION) and final stage mkdir/chown line; host copy adds ARG VERSION and chown app:app /app
findings.obligation: Container build under CI BuildKit (buildx, --build-arg VERSION) produces a runnable image; green observation must cover the committed Dockerfile
findings.observation: Committed Dockerfile publish stage uses /p:Version=VERSION with no ARG in that stage; the host green run used a copy that re-declares ARG VERSION and adds chown app:app /app, because the legacy builder did not reproduce CI behaviour. Without the re-declare SDK 11 fails MSB4044 (host). /app ownership: committed file chowns only /app/logs and /app/data. Both reliances are pre-existing; S3 changed only lines 5 and 13. Docker/BuildKit behaviour relied on is UNVERIFIED in this environment (no buildx installed). Green evidence therefore does not cover the committed bytes.
findings.remediation: Non-blocking for S3 craft: the ci_docker.yml check step is the first observer of the committed bytes under BuildKit, so confirm its CI run on main before completion. Preferably make both dependencies explicit in the Dockerfile (ARG VERSION in publish; chown of /app) and observe with buildx.

findings.location: Dockerfile final stage apt block: $(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME")-pgdg main
findings.obligation: Distro dependence: no apt package name or codename in the Dockerfile may break on the new aspnet:11.0 base
findings.observation: aspnet:11.0 base is Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (host container os-release, observed). The PGDG codename is derived at build time, and apt packages curl, gnupg, postgresql-client are resolved on that base. Host local build exit 0 observed at 12:24, so this passed once. node-builder stage is node bookworm-slim and unchanged by S3. No hard-coded codename in the file. Dependence on apt.postgresql.org carrying the 26.04 codename is external and unverified beyond that one build.
findings.remediation: Non-blocking: CI ci_docker.yml run on main is the observer. If the PGDG codename is missing, pin the PostgreSQL client package source explicitly.
